content:
We have leftInverse_of_surjective_of_rightInverse and rightInverse_of_injective_of_leftInverse. Mathlib duplicates these, but under different names, using dot notation (it has RightInverse.leftInverse_of_surjective' , RightInverse.leftInverse_of_injective`as the names for these, as well as LeftInverse -> RightInverse versions).

Putting aside the fact that I am not sure we should have both RightInverse and LeftInverse (but that is best discussed elsewhere), I do think the dot notation forms are useful. Also, as I say there is proof duplication (and I slightly prefer the Mathlib proofs which are to my eye more economical ways of stating the same thing). I have to imagine this duplication is unintentional. Is this a problem for mathlib, as a consumer of Std, or a problem for Std (as it could be improved with slight proof tidying + more dot notation).

(I don't think we have Surjective.leftInverse_of_rightInverse and things like that, but incidentally you could also imagine that. But it's a bit like how we lack LeftInverse.surjective and RightInverse.injective in core...)

It might be that this is best tidied up as part of rationalising the approach to RightInverse and LeftInverse. But I wanted to raise it - because the fact that leftInverse_of_surjective_of_rightInverse was news to me until just now and I look at this part of the library all the time. It's confusing, not least because of the different ways of saying the same thing.
I am raising this in #lean4 rather than #mathlib4 because as I say I think it is arguably an issue in Std/Core.
